doc: THE LDTK AUTHORING CONTRACT — one file, two readers.
Rust PROVES it: `contract::prover` builds each entity from this table, runs the
real `entity_to_runtime`, and asserts every claim here in both directions — a
`required` field whose removal does NOT fail the converter is a test failure, and
so is an entity that fails to convert when only its declared-required fields are
present. So this file cannot claim a requirement the parser does not enforce, and
the parser cannot enforce a requirement this file does not declare.
Python ENFORCES it: `validate_rules.entity_contract` reads this same file with no
cargo in sight, which is the whole point — the agent this engine exists to serve
has no build lease and could not otherwise discover any of it.
Adding a required field is therefore ONE edit here plus the parser change. There is

keys.presence: required = the converter refuses the entity without it. recommended = the converter accepts absence, but every author wants it (authoring warns). optional = silent.
keys.on_invalid: what the RUNTIME does with a value this field's declared grammar rejects. refused = the converter returns Err. silent_default = the converter accepts it and quietly substitutes `default` — authoring treats this as an ERROR anyway, because a typo here is invisible and there is no extension story. open = the fallthrough is a real extension point with real consumers, so authoring says nothing.
keys.values / patterns: the closed literal set and the regex grammars that complete it. Both empty means the field has no declared grammar.
keys.sample / poison: prober-only. `sample` is a value that must convert; `poison` overrides the default illegal value the prober pokes with.
keys.undeclared fields: carry no rule. `name`, free-form ids and pure tuning numbers are deliberately absent.

entities.note: the RESET volume (the pit floor). A surface that HURTS is a DamageVolume.

fields.name: tier
fields.note: which blink upgrade dissolves this wall

fields.name: impulseX
fields.note: horizontal launch impulse; the pad has no default and the converter refuses without it

fields.name: impulseY
fields.note: vertical launch impulse (negative is UP)

fields.name: trigger
fields.note: OnStand needs a collision that blocks movement

fields.name: respawn
fields.note: `AfterSeconds` pairs with a positive `respawn_seconds`; `AfterSeconds:<n>` is the legacy inline spelling

entities.note: target_room / target_zone pairing and arrival geometry are checked by the room-graph rules in validate.py; they are not converter refusals.

fields.name: activation
fields.note: REFUSED since 2026-08-21, and the note it replaces said why: `anything the converter does not recognise silently becomes a Door, so edgeexit is a door and nothing says so`. LDtk types this field as free-text String with default Door, so an author spells it from memory -- which is also why the shipped worlds read 127 Door / 24 EdgeExit / 0 Walk. One parse now owns the mapping (LoadingZoneActivation::from_authored); it trims and lowercases, so case and stray whitespace are forgiven and a genuine typo is an error in both the converter and the validator. The old match accepted `walk` but not `edgeexit` -- one variant forgiving, its sibling not.

fields.name: path_points
fields.note: fewer than two parseable points is not an error at runtime — the hazard simply never moves

fields.name: points
fields.note: semicolon-separated `x,y` pairs in level-local pixels

fields.name: points
fields.note: a CLOSED chain needs three; author floors left-to-right, the winding is the one-sidedness

fields.name: radius
fields.note: the marker's centre is the loop centre; the polygon is generated at conversion

fields.name: orientation
fields.note: named by the two surfaces it joins, in travel order

fields.name: kind
fields.note: a PropRegistry sprite id. Decoration only — a Prop never grows an Interactable.

fields.name: character_id
fields.note: the catalog character this NPC wears. Unlike EnemySpawn the converter TOLERATES absence — the display name then stands in — but every NpcSpawn in the tree authors one.

fields.name: kind
fields.note: an unrecognised kind becomes PickupKind::Custom, and `collect_pickups` has NO arm for Custom — the pickup disappears on touch and grants nothing. `currancy:1` is a working pickup that does nothing.

fields.name: reward
fields.note: same grammar and the same silent hole as PickupSpawn.kind. Absent is legal: a chest with no reward.

fields.name: held_item
fields.note: a held-item registry id (`bomb`, `grapple`, `gun_sword`, ...). An UNREGISTERED id is tolerated at spawn — the item just does not appear — so only emptiness is refused.

fields.name: pair
fields.note: which portal pair THIS gun owns. A gun toggles between the two ends of its own pair and never leaves it, so two pickups on different pairs are two independently coloured guns (one blue/orange, one whatever pair 1 renders as). A value outside the range WRAPS rather than refusing the room — a mistyped number should hand the author a differently coloured gun to notice, not a level that fails to load — and a value that is not a number at all falls back to the default pair 0.

fields.name: color
fields.note: names the channel; `c<n>` addresses an indexed channel

fields.name: normal
fields.note: the surface the portal sits ON — up = floor, down = ceiling

fields.name: dir
fields.note: an unrecognised direction silently becomes `up`, which is also the value an author most often means, so the mistake is invisible

fields.name: character_id
fields.note: which catalog creature this placement puts down. The display name is a LABEL; the engine reading it as the art identity was a coincidence, and this field is refused when absent so the next placement cannot inherit that.

fields.name: brain
fields.note: a bare id becomes CharacterBrain::Custom(id), which providers really do match on (`mary_o_snake`, `sanic_badnik`, `combatant`) — so an unrecognised value is an EXTENSION, not a typo, and authoring stays quiet. `Patrol:<id>` is retired: author `path_ref` and clear this.

fields.name: path_ref
fields.note: a native EntityRef at the KinematicPath this body patrols. A ref that names something that is not a KinematicPath in the SAME active area is refused, never degraded to `stands still`.

fields.name: respawn
fields.note: absent leaves the archetype's policy, which is what every level authored before the field existed

fields.name: facing
fields.note: which way this occurrence starts. Facing is PLACEMENT context: the character and its brain are reusable, and two instances of the same pair may enter a room looking opposite ways. Absent or blank keeps the historical Right/+1 default; a misspelling is refused rather than silently changing initial locomotion.

fields.name: brain
fields.note: an unrecognised value becomes BossBrain::Custom(label), which `boss_encounter::behavior` genuinely consumes

fields.name: text
fields.note: absent, the label renders the literal string `DebugLabel`

fields.name: category
fields.note: `Custom` is a real category an author picks on purpose, which is exactly why a misspelt `Enmy` landing there is invisible

entities.note: a platform states exactly ONE motion. sweep_dx, path_id and loop_dy are three answers to the same question and the converter refuses more than one.

fields.name: sweep_dx
fields.note: a signed horizontal DELTA, so it takes no level offset

fields.name: path_id
fields.note: the path carries its own speed, so authoring `speed` beside it is refused rather than ignored

fields.name: speed
fields.note: pixels per second for a sweep or a wrapping shaft. Undeclared until 2026-08-15, when the prover caught `path_id` naming it as a conflict while no field of that name existed — so the converter read a field the contract could not describe and no authoring tool could offer. `open` with no grammar because the converter genuinely has no rule here: any float parses, and a negative one is carried through rather than refused or defaulted. A path carries its own speed, hence the conflict.

fields.name: loop_dy
fields.note: the signed height of a wrapping shaft (positive travels DOWN). Zero is refused: a shaft with no span never moves.

fields.name: loop_min_y
fields.note: a POSITION (it takes the level offset), naming where the wrapping shaft starts. On its own it describes no motion, so it is refused without loop_dy.

fields.name: action
fields.note: the converter passes this straight through into the interaction payload and cares about none of it. `encounter::systems` recognises the listed actions and IGNORES the rest, so an unlisted action is a switch that does nothing — but the refusal, if one is ever wanted, belongs to that consumer and not here.

fields.name: on_activate
fields.note: one authored command call — `<domain>.<verb> <arg>…`, whitespace-separated — performed when the switch is activated. Read off the raw LdtkProject by `world::authored_switch_commands`, not by this converter, and PREPARED once when the room is read: the id is checked against the published command catalog, the arity against the descriptor, and a `placement:`/`encounter:` reference is minted through SimId's own constructor. ABSENT means the switch belongs to its other consumers (encounter arming, reset, the sand sim) — which is why it is optional. A line this composition cannot perform is dropped with a warning at prepare time rather than on the tick.

entities.note: read off the raw LdtkProject by its own consumer; the converter emits nothing, so it declares no field rules.
read off the raw LdtkProject by `crate::encounter`; the converter emits nothing.
read off the raw LdtkProject by its own consumers; the converter emits nothing. TWO consumers: the encounter seal (phase-driven, no gated_by) and the authored condition gate (gated_by present).

fields.name: gated_by
fields.note: names a world-fact flag; the wall stands until `world.flag_set(<gated_by>)` is satisfied. ABSENT means this wall belongs to the encounter consumer or is inert - which is why it is optional and why an unknown flag is not refused: a flag that has never been set is a legitimate authored state, so refusing unknown names would refuse every wall gated on a fact the run has not reached yet.
